cards.prose: The prayer asks that the Father's name be hallowed, and the prophet shows whose name that is and why it needs hallowing: the house of Yashar'el (Israel) carried it into the nations and profaned it there. Yahuah (the LORD) says he will act for the sake of that name, so the petition asks him to do what he has already said he would do.
cards.member_phrase: but for mine holy name’s sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) says he will act for his own holy name, which his scattered people profaned among the nations.

cards.prose: Asking to be forgiven was never a new thing laid on the disciples. Once a year the people were told the priest makes atonement so they may be clean before Yahuah (the LORD), and the petition about debts comes out of that same need to stand clean before him. The words go on to say the one asking must also release his own debtors.
cards.member_phrase: to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before Yahuah (LORD).
cards.member_sentence: The yearly atonement was how the people were made clean from all their sins before Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.prose: Here the master says *I forgave thee all that debt* and then calls the servant wicked because he would not show his own fellow the same. The parable puts a face on what the verse says plainly: forgiveness received from the Father is meant to be passed on, and the man who refuses answers for his refusal.
cards.member_phrase: O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me:
cards.member_sentence: A servant who was forgiven a great debt is called wicked for refusing his fellow what he himself received.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) says he redeemed these people, and still woe comes on them because they fled from him and spoke lies against him. Being redeemed did not hold them in place once they walked off. That is the weight behind the second half of the verse about forgiveness: what the Father gives, a man can lose by how he turns.
cards.member_phrase: though I have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lies against me.
cards.member_sentence: Though redeemed, the people fled and spoke lies against Yahuah (the LORD), and woe follows them.

cards.prose: The prophet says a man counted righteous who turns to iniquity finds his earlier righteousness is not remembered, and in his sin he dies. Forgiveness in the verse stands on the same terms. It is kept as a man goes on in the Father's way, and it is not a standing that cannot be forfeited.
cards.member_phrase: when the righteous turneth away from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, and doeth according to all the abominations that the wicked man doeth, shall he live? All his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned
cards.member_sentence: A righteous man who turns to iniquity has his past righteousness set aside, and dies in his sin.

cards.prose: The prophet sets the matter both ways: yesterday's righteousness does not deliver a man on the day he transgresses, and the wicked who turns is not undone by his old wickedness. So the Father's forgiveness in the verse is spoken to the day a man is standing in, and a refusal to forgive today is not covered by obedience before it.
cards.member_phrase: The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression
cards.member_sentence: The righteousness of the righteous does not deliver him on the day he transgresses.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) says this to Moses after the people made the calf, and it is said of those who stand written in his book. Sin against him can cost a name its place there. That is why the Father's word that he will not forgive the one who will not forgive is no figure of speech.
cards.member_sentence: Whoever has sinned against Yahuah (the LORD) he will blot out of his book, which is a real loss.

cards.prose: The psalmist is praying for certain men to lose their place in the book of the living and to stand outside the company of the righteous, so that book is no picture and a name can be taken from it. Matthew's verse draws a line in the same place, between the man who is forgiven and the man who is not, and the line follows whether he forgives.
cards.member_sentence: The book of the living is real, and the psalmist asks that men be blotted out of it and not written with the righteous.

cards.prose: If a man sins on purpose after he has come to know the truth, no sacrifice remains for those sins. That is the door the second half of the verse shuts: the one who knows what the Father asks and still refuses to forgive has chosen the sin, and has no sacrifice left to cover it.
cards.member_sentence: Wilful sin after the truth is known leaves no sacrifice remaining for those sins.

cards.prose: At the close of the same sermon Yahusha (Jesus) says that calling him by his title does not open the kingdom, only doing the will of the Father does. Forgiving men is part of that will, so the warning here and the warning there come from one mouth about one man, the one who says the right words and does not do them.
cards.member_phrase: but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.
cards.member_sentence: Saying his title is not enough for the kingdom, only doing the will of the Father is.

cards.prose: John says the Father is *faithful and just to forgive us our sins* when we confess them, so forgiveness is met with something on our side. Yahusha (Jesus) names another thing on our side in this verse, the forgiving of men, and neither one is a wage. Each is how a person stands when he asks to be forgiven.
cards.member_sentence: Forgiveness comes to the one who confesses, so it is received in a certain posture and not apart from it.

cards.prose: Giving to the poor brother is commanded here, with a warning not to *harden thine heart* or *shut thine hand*. So when Yahusha (Jesus) says to take heed how alms are given, he is not setting the giving aside. He is guarding the heart the commandment speaks to, so the gift is not turned into a show.
cards.member_phrase: thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother:
cards.member_sentence: The Torah commands an open hand to the poor brother and forbids a hardened heart.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) built provision for the poor into the edges of the field, the corners left unreaped and the gleanings left on the ground. Nobody sounded a trumpet for it, since the poor simply came and took what was left for them. That is the quiet, ordinary giving the verse has in mind.
cards.member_phrase: thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest.
cards.member_sentence: The corners of the field and the gleanings were left standing for the poor as part of the harvest.

cards.prose: A sheaf forgotten in the field is left where it lies, for the stranger, the fatherless and the widow, and the owner is told not to go back for it. Giving that nobody watches is already in the Torah, and the blessing named belongs to Yahuah (the LORD), not to onlookers.
cards.member_phrase: thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) may bless thee in all the work of thine hands.
cards.member_sentence: A forgotten sheaf is left for the stranger, the fatherless and the widow, and Yahuah (the LORD) blesses the giver.

cards.prose: The blessing falls on the one who *considereth the poor*, and the deliverance in time of trouble comes from Yahuah (the LORD), not from men watching. That shows where the reward lies. A man who gives to be seen has traded the reward of the Father for a lesser one.
cards.member_sentence: Blessing and deliverance in trouble belong to the man who considers the poor.

cards.prose: Earlier in the sermon the light is to shine so that men see good works and glorify the Father, and here alms are not to be done *to be seen of them*. The two do not fight. In the first the glory goes to the Father, in the second it goes to the doer, and what settles it is who the seen thing points to.
cards.member_sentence: Good works are seen so that the Father is glorified, which is the opposite of giving to be seen.

cards.prose: Solomon prays in front of the whole congregation with his hands spread out, and the prayer is right. So the verse about the street corners is not against praying in the open. It is against praying in order to be seen, and the difference lies in who the praying is for.
cards.member_phrase: in the presence of all the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel), and spread forth his hands toward heaven:
cards.member_sentence: Solomon prayed openly before the whole congregation at the altar, so public prayer is not what is forbidden.

cards.prose: The same men who were taught to pray in secret later continued *with one accord* in prayer together, with the women and the family of Yahusha (Jesus). The shut door is about the heart, not a ban on praying with others, and here the company is joined in a single purpose before the Father.
cards.member_sentence: The disciples continued together in prayer and supplication with one accord, so praying with others is not ruled out.

cards.prose: Prayers stand here beside the teaching, the fellowship and the breaking of bread as part of how that company lived. Yahusha (Jesus) is not ruling out shared prayer. He is dealing with why a man prays before others, whether it is for them or for the Father.
cards.member_sentence: Prayers were one of the things the first company held to steadily, along with teaching, fellowship and bread.

cards.prose: When they lifted up their voice together, what they said was spoken to the Maker of heaven, earth and sea, and nothing in it was aimed at listeners. A company can pray aloud without performing, and that was the very thing the hypocrites on the street corners had lost.
cards.member_phrase: they lifted up their voice to Elohim (God) with one accord, and said,
cards.member_sentence: The company raised their voice together to the one who made heaven, earth and sea.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) prays aloud with a crowd around him, thanking the Father who had heard him, and then says why: *that they may believe that thou hast sent me* (John 11:42). His prayer is spoken to the Father first and heard by others second, which is the order the verse about the street corners turns on.
cards.member_phrase: Yahusha (Jesus) lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) prayed aloud before the crowd, speaking to the Father who had heard him.

cards.prose: A man who knows he is already searched and known has no one to impress. The psalm goes on, *there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O Yahuah (LORD), thou knowest it altogether* (Psalm 139:4), and that is why a prayer needs neither an audience nor padding.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) has searched and known the one who prays, so there is nothing to show him.

cards.prose: Moses reminds the people that the one they have been treating so badly is their father, who bought them, made them and established them. So when Yahusha (Jesus) teaches them to say Our Father, he is not bringing in a new name for the Maker. Yashar'el (Israel) was already told he is their father, and told it as a rebuke.
cards.member_phrase: is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee?
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) is called the father who bought, made and established his people.

cards.prose: The bread asked for this day is the bread Yahuah (the LORD) rained from heaven, gathered a day at a time. He gave it to prove whether the people would walk in his law, so the daily bread in the prayer comes with the Father's instruction attached and not apart from it.
cards.member_phrase: the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.
cards.member_sentence: The manna came a day at a time to prove whether the people would walk in his law.

cards.prose: A man here asks for neither poverty nor riches, only the food fitting for him. That is the size of what the prayer asks for, bread for the day and no more, put in the same plain terms by someone who wanted to be kept from both extremes.
cards.member_sentence: The wise man asks for neither poverty nor riches, only food convenient for him.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) answered the tempter with these words in the wilderness, so he knows what bread is for. The prayer asks for bread, and the answer he gave says a man needs more than bread: the word that comes out of the mouth of Elohim (God). The two belong together in one request.
cards.member_phrase: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of Elohim (God).
cards.member_sentence: A man lives by every word from the mouth of Elohim (God), not by bread alone.

cards.prose: The one teaching the prayer had just been led into the wilderness and tempted, so he is not speaking of something far from himself. He was led there by the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) and still came through, which is what the petition asks of the Father for his disciples: to be brought through and delivered from evil.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) had himself just been led into the wilderness to be tempted, and knows the road he teaches them to pray about.

cards.prose: Here is the answer to what the petition asks: the Father is faithful, and he does not let temptation press past what a man can bear but makes a way out beside it. The prayer asks to be delivered from evil, and this verse says what deliverance looks like in the middle of the trial.
cards.member_phrase: Elohim (God) is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.
cards.member_sentence: Elohim (God) is faithful and does not let the temptation go beyond what a man can bear, but makes a way out.

cards.prose: James shuts off a wrong reading of the petition. Asking not to be led into temptation does not mean the Father tempts anyone, since he cannot be tempted with evil and tempts no man. The prayer asks him to keep his children clear of the temptation that comes from elsewhere.
cards.member_phrase: for Elohim (God) cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:
cards.member_sentence: Elohim (God) cannot be tempted with evil and tempts no man, so the petition cannot mean he leads anyone into evil.

cards.prose: The Torah itself commands a day when the people afflict their souls, so fasting is not something Yahusha (Jesus) invents or sets aside. What he corrects is the sad face worn for others to see. A commanded fast is kept before Yahuah (the LORD), and putting on a look for men makes it theirs.
cards.member_phrase: there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto Yahuah (LORD).
cards.member_sentence: The Torah commands a day of atonement on which the people afflict their souls.

cards.prose: The prophet calls the elders and all the people of the land together to sanctify a fast and cry out to Yahuah (the LORD). A fast kept openly by the whole land is right when it is held for him. So the Father who sees in secret is not against fasting together, only against the face put on for onlookers.
cards.member_phrase: Sanctify ye a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land
cards.member_sentence: Joel calls the whole land to sanctify a fast and cry to Yahuah (the LORD) together.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) fasted forty days and nights in the wilderness, and the account has him alone, mentioning only the hunger that came after. He teaches fasting as a man who has done it in the way he describes, before the Father and not before onlookers.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) himself fasted forty days and nights, and was hungry only afterward.

cards.prose: Riches do not help on the day of wrath, and righteousness does. That is the reason to lay up treasure where moth, rust and thieves cannot reach it: a day comes when only what was laid up in righteousness is of any use.
cards.member_sentence: Riches are of no use on the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.

cards.prose: The wise man says not to wear yourself out to get rich, and gives the reason in the next line: *riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven* (Proverbs 23:5). Treasure on earth leaves on its own, which is why moth, rust and thieves are named in the verse.
cards.member_sentence: Riches grow wings and fly away, so the wise man says not to labour to be rich.

cards.prose: The psalmist tells his hearer not to be afraid when another grows rich, and says why: *when he dieth he shall carry nothing away* (Psalm 49:17), and his glory does not follow him down. What a man stores here stays here, so the verse sends the treasure to the one place that does not decay.
cards.member_sentence: A rich man's glory does not go down with him at death, so no one need fear his wealth.

cards.prose: Luke carries the same teaching and says how the treasure is laid up: by selling and giving alms. The treasure in heaven is made out of open-handed giving to the poor, the very command the first verses of this chapter were guarding, so the alms and the treasure are one subject.
cards.member_phrase: provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.
cards.member_sentence: Selling and giving alms is how the treasure in the heavens is provided, where no thief or moth reaches it.

cards.prose: The first of the ten words already says there is no room for a second master. When Yahusha (Jesus) puts mammon beside Elohim (God) as a rival to be served, he is saying money can become the other god, and the commandment stands against it as it stood against the gods of the nations.
cards.member_sentence: No other gods before Yahuah (the LORD) is the commandment behind the refusal to serve two masters.

cards.prose: This verse says Yahuah (the LORD) is one, and the next line asks for love *with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might* (Deuteronomy 6:5). A man cannot give all of that to him and keep a share for mammon, so loving the one and despising the other is this command put to money.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) is one, and the whole heart belongs to him, which leaves no share for another master.

cards.prose: Elijah asks the people how long they will limp between two sides, Yahuah (the LORD) or Baal, and they answer him not a word. That is the picture behind two masters. A man who tries to hold both ends up silent when asked whom he follows, and the verse says he will love one and despise the other.
cards.member_phrase: How long halt ye between two opinions? if Yahuah (LORD) be Elohim (God), follow him: but if Baal, then follow him.
cards.member_sentence: Elijah demands that the people choose between Yahuah (the LORD) and Baal, and they cannot answer.

cards.prose: The proverb shows what a good eye is: the man with a bountiful eye gives of his bread to the poor. So when the verse says the body is full of light if the eye is single, it is speaking of an open-handed heart and not of eyesight.
cards.member_sentence: A bountiful eye is one that gives bread to the poor, and it is blessed.

cards.prose: The proverb's evil eye belongs to a grudging man who sets out food while *his heart is not with thee* (Proverbs 23:7). That is the eye behind the body full of darkness in the verse: a stingy, grasping heart and not a failing of sight.
cards.member_sentence: The man with an evil eye is a grudging host, whose food the wise are told not to desire.

cards.prose: Moses uses the evil eye in a command about the poor: do not count down to the year of release and give nothing, or he cries to Yahuah (the LORD) against you and it is sin. The same Torah that commands the open hand names the closed eye as sin, and the single eye is the one that obeys.
cards.member_phrase: and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought; and he cry unto Yahuah (LORD) against thee, and it be sin unto thee.
cards.member_sentence: An eye evil against a poor brother who is given nothing is sin in the Torah.

cards.prose: Here the evil eye belongs to the man in a hurry to be rich, who does not see that poverty is coming for him. A greedy eye chasing money leaves the body dark, which is the opposite of the single eye that sees the poor and gives, and the proverb ends with the loss he cannot see.
cards.member_sentence: The man in haste to be rich has an evil eye and does not see that poverty is coming.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) gives the beast its food, and even the young ravens that cry. The birds in the verse are not a sentimental picture. They are his own care, already sung in the psalms, and the man asked to look at them is asked to look at what the psalmist had praised.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) gives food to the beast and to the young ravens that cry.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) answers Job out of the whirlwind by asking where he was when the earth was laid. The one who set the foundations in place is the one the verse says feeds the fowls, so a man's worry about his food is held up against the size of the one who cares.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) asks Job where he was when the foundations of the earth were laid, and shows whose hands hold creation.

cards.prose: The psalm shows how wide his feeding goes: he sends springs into the valleys and makes grass grow on the mountains, so the creatures are fed by a whole arrangement he made and keeps. If he supplies water and grass for them, the man who looks to him for food is not forgotten.
cards.member_sentence: The springs sent into the valleys show the Father's provision reaching every creature, which the birds stand for.

cards.prose: Solomon asked for an understanding heart and not for long life or riches, and Elohim (God) was pleased and then gave him the riches he did not ask for as well. That is seeking first and having it added: the thing sought was right judgment, and the rest came on top of it.
cards.member_phrase: Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself
cards.member_sentence: Solomon asked for understanding and not for riches, and the riches were given to him as well.

cards.prose: Delight set on Yahuah (the LORD) comes first in the psalm, and what the heart wants follows. It has the same order as the verse: the kingdom and righteousness first, then the things a man would otherwise worry about added to him. The giving rests on where the delight is placed.
cards.member_sentence: Delight in Yahuah (the LORD) comes first, and he gives the desires of the heart after it.

cards.prose: The man who hungers and thirsts after righteousness is told he will be filled, and the verse in this chapter tells the anxious man to seek the kingdom and his righteousness first. The hunger that is blessed is the same seeking, turned from worry over food and clothes to the thing that fills.
cards.member_sentence: Those who hunger and thirst after righteousness are blessed and will be filled, which is the seeking of the kingdom first.
